t:
Section 508(k)(4) of the Federal Crop Insurance Act (7 U.S.C. 1508(k)(4)) (as amended by section 12015) is amended—
    (1) in subparagraph (A), by striking “Except as provided in subparagraph (B)” and inserting “Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph”; and 
    (2) by adding at the end the following:“(E) Reimbursement rate reduction.—In the case of a policy of additional coverage that received a rate of reimbursement for administrative and operating costs for the 2008 reinsurance year, for each of the 2009 and subsequent reinsurance years, the reimbursement rate for administrative and operating costs shall be 2.3 percentage points below the rates in effect as of the date of enactment of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008 for all crop insurance policies used to define loss ratio, except that only ½ of the reduction shall apply in a reinsurance year to the total premium written in a State in which the State loss ratio is greater than 1.2.“(F) Reimbursement rate for area policies and plans of insurance.—Notwithstanding subparagraphs (A) through (E), for each of the 2009 and subsequent reinsurance years, the reimbursement rate for area policies and plans of insurance widely available as of the date of enactment of this subparagraph shall be 12 percent of the premium used to define loss ratio for that reinsurance year.”.

fable.w: This section amends the Federal Crop Insurance Act to fix statutory reimbursement rates for administrative and operating costs of crop insurance policies. The tempting reading is that references to insurers and States imply outside involvement, but they only describe who the rates apply to and how the rate is calculated. There is no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: the reimbursement rate for administrative and operating costs shall be 2.3 percentage points below the rates in effect as of the date of enactment of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008

opus.w: The amendment sets reimbursement rates for administrative and operating costs directly in the statute. It does not require or allow consultation with outside parties, public comment, hearings, advisory committees, rulemaking or legal challenges. Private insurers are affected by these rates, but they play no part in setting them, so this is not participation.
opus.s: the reimbursement rate for area policies and plans of insurance widely available as of the date of enactment of this subparagraph shall be 12 percent of the premium used to define loss ratio for that reinsurance year.
opus.b:
I'm labelling this **No**: the section sets crop insurance reimbursement rates directly in the statute, and no one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

The tempting reading is that it involves participation because it concerns private insurance companies and their reimbursement for administrative costs. That fails the definition. The amendment fixes the numbers itself (a 2.3-point reduction and a 12 percent rate). It doesn't require consultation, a comment period, a hearing, an advisory body, rulemaking authority or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a formula for calculating reimbursement rates for crop insurance policies. While it references 'State loss ratio,' this is a data point used in an automatic calculation, not a requirement for consultation or coordination with state governments or other outside parties. There is no mechanism for outside input, public comment, or advisory involvement in the decision-making process described.
qwen_chat.s: except that only ½ of the reduction shall apply in a reinsurance year to the total premium written in a State in which the State loss ratio is greater than 1.2
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "State loss ratio" and "State," it involves coordination with state governments. However, the text only uses state data as a variable in a formula for calculating federal reimbursement rates. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from state officials or the public before making the decision. The decision is purely mathematical and administrative based on pre-existing data.
